Maisie Filler, from Florida, is a standout University of Florida golfer who joined the Arcis team as a brand ambassador in 2024. A four-time SEC Golfer of the Week and Second Team All-American, she has competed at the Augusta National Women’s Amateur and is working toward earning her LPGA Tour card. As an Arcis ambassador, she champions growing access to golf and represents the next generation of female players.

Gina Kim, born in Albuquerque and raised in Chapel Hill, NC, began playing golf at seven and became the state’s top junior golfer by 14 before starring at Duke University and winning an NCAA Championship. Renowned for her precise ball striking and calm course management, she turned professional in 2022, won on the Epson Tour as a rookie, and now leads the 2025 Race for the Card. She joined the Arcis team in 2025, representing elite performance and passion for the game.

Mackenzie Lee, from North Little Rock, Arkansas, is one of SMU’s standout junior golfers and a rising star in collegiate golf. She holds multiple SMU records—including lowest career scoring average and most rounds of par or better—and has posted several top-five finishes. In 2025, she joined the Arcis team, bringing consistent scoring, mental toughness, and national amateur success to the roster.

MacyPate is from Winston-Salem, North Carolina, where she was introduced to golf at a young age and quickly drawn to the sport's competitive nature. Pateset herself apart in high school by shooting a historic 57, the lowest scoreever recorded in North Carolina high school golf, along with multiple standout performances in junior and amateur events. She has continued that momentum atWake Forest University, where she has quickly established herself as one of the program’s top players

Sophia Popov, born in Boston and raised in Germany, committed to golf at 14 and became one of USC’s most accomplished collegiate players. Known for her precise iron play and strategic approach, she had a breakout season in 2020 with a major championship victory after overcoming significant health challenges. In 2025, she joined the Arcis ambassador team, bringing major-winning experience, leadership, and inspiration to the community.

Bailey Tardy grew up in Georgia and discovered golf at seven, inspired by her father’s encouragement. She went on to play for the University of Georgia and became known for her powerful, confident style and elite ball-striking, ranking among the LPGA Tour’s longest hitters. In 2025, she joined the Arcis ambassador team, bringing southern grit and rising-star momentum to the roster.
